record.context_brief: The maximal length of an integer set
record.original_question: Is it true that for n 7, any n-element set of integers is isomorphic (in Freiman's sense) to a subset of [0; 2n 2]? For any integer n 2 the set f0; 1; 2; 4; : : :; 2n 2g is \linear" (has Freiman's dimension one) and not contained in an arithmetic progression with di erence larger than 1, hence it is not isomorphic to a set of integers of length smaller than 2n 2. It is conjectured in that this is the extremal case; that is, in any class of isomorphic n-element sets there is a set of length at most 2n 2. Note, that all Sidon sets with the same number of elements are isomorphic to each other, and it is well-known that for N large enough the interval [0; N] contains a Sidon set of cardinality about p N. Thus, any n-element Sidon set is isomorphic to a subset of [0; n2(1 + o(1))]. For n 6, however, this n2(1 + o(1)) turns out to be larger, than 2n 2: more precisely, [0; 2n 2] does not contain an n-element Sidon set. This explains the restriction n 7 above.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Two finite sets of integers A and B are called Freiman isomorphic (of order 2) if there is a bijection φ: A → B such that for all a₁,a₂,a₃,a₄ ∈ A one has a₁ + a₂ = a₃ + a₄ if and only if φ(a₁) + φ(a₂) = φ(a₃) + φ(a₄). The length of a finite set of integers S is max S − min S. A finite set of integers is said to have Freiman dimension one if it is Freiman isomorphic to a subset of ℤ (equivalently, of an arithmetic progression with common difference 1) but not to a subset of a higher-dimensional generalized arithmetic progression in a non-degenerate way.

For every integer n ≥ 2, the set {0, 1, 2, 4, 6, …, 2n − 2} (i.e. {0, 1} together with the even numbers up to 2n − 2) has Freiman dimension one, has length 2n − 2, and is not Freiman isomorphic to any set of integers of length smaller than 2n − 2.

Prove or disprove: for every integer n ≥ 7, every n-element set of integers is Freiman isomorphic (in the sense above) to a subset of the interval [0, 2n − 2]. Equivalently, in every Freiman-isomorphism class of n-element integer sets there exists a representative of length at most 2n − 2.

Standard references on Freiman's theorem and additive combinatorics discuss related sumset and dimension results but do not record a resolution of this specific extremal-length conjecture, so its status is taken as unknown.
